title: Localization of an internal finite basis with its specified scalar map
statement:
Let $C$ be a small site whose abelian sheaves carry the sheafified tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], let $t$ be a global section of $R$, and let $I$ be a finite set. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Suppose global sections $b_i$ of $T$ give an $R$-module isomorphism
$$q:R^{\oplus I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}T,\qquad (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_i\varphi(a_i)b_i.$$
Let $j_R:R\to A$ and $j_T:T\to B$ be morphisms of commutative ring objects exhibiting localization at $t$ and $\varphi(t)$, respectively. Explicitly, $j_R(t)$ is invertible and every ring map $R\to D$ making $t$ invertible factors uniquely through $j_R$; impose the analogous condition on $j_T$ and $\varphi(t)$.

There is a unique ring map $\varphi_t:A\to B$ with $\varphi_tj_R=j_T\varphi$. There is an $A$-module isomorphism
$$q_t:A^{\oplus I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_t}B,\qquad (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_i\varphi_t(a_i)j_T(b_i).$$
It satisfies $q_tj_R^{\oplus I}=j_Tq$ and is the unique $A$-linear map satisfying this equation. No injectivity of $\varphi$ or nonzero-divisor hypothesis on $t$ is assumed.
